## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [22. November 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.65
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.65
- Datum: 22.11.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Rio, Central Hôtel
Rio, 22.11.40
Dear Hanna & Manfred, Just now your telegram about the new
address - I am happy to know you well but rather angry about
Salmon's thoughtlessness not to see that the child writes re-
gularly and glad to know that a letter of Eva's must reach you
one of these days, sent by my sister-in-law with her explanation
about reading Eva's letter. We have also had no direct news from
her and it is fortunate that my sister-in-law kept me in-
formed and that I always wrote you her impressions. - About the
new living arrangement of Manfred's I send my best wishes,
all included in the one that he may be able to live there for
the duration without having to change, and that he can keep up
quiet long weekends at Bath. - About E's visa we cabled you
again yesterday. The explanation is that the second person for whom
Stefan had also secured (or thought to have secured) a visa to Argentine
from England, had cabled about difficulties in getting it in spite
of telegraphic instructions from Buenos Aires, and that led to the
second cable from there, ordering the Arg. consul in London to
give at least a tourist visa to those two. But maybe Fr.
owing to his protestant faith had less difficulties than the
other, the former editor of Cherido in Amsterdam who is now in
England. You did not write anything about your brother, so I
am afraid it is not yet settled. Tell him, if he likes to
take Stefan's manuscript case for the journey. It is always useful
and I am sorry I did not insist on taking it. - Our plans keep
on changing. The newest idea is to stay here in Rio until
the end of January and then go to USA for 3 months in-
stead of packing up again in a few weeks to go to the mountains.
Until now it is not at all hot in spite of splendid weather. Ste-
fan wants me to apologise to Mama because I wrote her that
it is now the rainy season - we have a large room with a big
covered terrace and no sun after 10 a.m., overlooking the bay and
catching every breeze of air, looking down directly on a bathing
beach, and the room even has a real writing-table. So I think we
shall stay here and see how long we like it. If it gets very hot
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelblichem Papier. Tinte violett. Die erste Seite ist gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
2) in the end, we think of going to USA, stopping first in Bahia and
Pernambuco, then take a boat to New Orleans and from there con-
tinue by train to Newyork, where we would look for a hotel or
small furnished service flat somewhere near the town but not in
the town itself, as there are too many friends and collegues
of Stefan's now in Newyork to allow him quiet working hours.
Needless to say that I shall then see much of Eva and give
detailed reports, but I am convinced already now that she
feels very much at home at New Rochelle as I take her
silence for a sign of being pleasantly occupied all the time.
I suppose it will be by the end of Jan., middle of Febr. that
we get to Newyork. - I hope that in Bath all goes smoothly in
spite of the many people and that none of the children or adults gives
you any trouble. Please tell Lizzy and Mannheims that for a long
time I intended to write them and that I have not given up the idea.
- It will soon be time to congratulate you and Mama to your
birthdays. I am sorry I cannot send any presents, I can only say
that it would give me pleasure if you get a beautiful present
for yourself or for each other in my name.
Kindest regards, also to Smolletto
Continuation of page 3
and kisses, wishes and best love,
Lotte.
shall go to Newyork. Personally I hate the idea of
changing and packing and further more the enormous family of Schnorrers
who expects us there will make the stay not restful. I want to work and
that has been nearly impossible through my lecture tour and the perpe-
tual voyages. Time goes on, a few days and I shall have been for the
last time in the fiftieth and I do not believe that I shall ever write
a book 'Life begins at Sixty'. Must I say that we think continually on you
and that all our wishes are over the ocean - this same ocean which
lies so blue and peaceful before our windows, while you have to stand
against all furies of this devil who wants to destroy our life. Yours ever
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf gelblichem Papier. Tinte violett. Die Seite enthält eine Fortsetzung und einen Nachtrag von Stefan Zweig.
Rückseite des dritten Blattes mit aufgelegter Farb- und Grauskala zur Archivierung.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift von Lotte und Stefan Zweig ist klar. Die Struktur des Briefes ist eindeutig.
